neighbours.label: a national or ethnic adjective naming a people inside a proper name or compound (African American, Mexican-American War, Polish Army); the same frames with a non-national adjective stay low
fire: The museum tells the story of African American soldiers in the Civil War.
Thousands of volunteers joined the Canadian Army in the first month.
Her grandfather fought in the Spanish-American War as a young man.
The festival celebrates Mexican American music and food every June.
The library holds letters written by Irish American immigrants in Boston.
After the war the jet was moved to the Polish Air Force Museum.
She wrote a history of African American churches in the South.
He studied the Italian-American community of New York in the 1920s.
quiet: The museum tells the story of young soldiers in the Civil War.
Thousands of volunteers joined the local militia in the first month.
Her grandfather fought in the long border war as a young man.
The festival celebrates local music and food every June.
The library holds letters written by poor immigrants in Boston.
After the war the jet was moved to the city's aviation museum.
She wrote a history of rural churches in the South.

notes: Card: peaks on ' African' x15, ' Canadian', ' Mexican', ' Polish', and ' the'/' its' before United States/US; the - pole promotes American/US.
